title: What If Pet Snakes Escaped Into a National Park? Florida's Did

scenes.text: What if pet snakes got loose in a swamp? The Everglades lost almost all its raccoons.
Burmese pythons from the pet trade took hold in the Everglades, and their numbers grew sharply after 2003.
Researchers drove more than 57,000 kilometers of park roads over 313 nights, counting mammals.
Raccoon sightings were down 99.3 percent. Opossums, 98.9. Bobcats, 87.5. No rabbits were seen.
The losses were worst in the south of the park, where the pythons first settled.
A pet becomes a predator no native animal evolved to face. The swamp is still counting the cost.

description:
What if pet snakes escaped into a swamp?
In Everglades National Park, mammal sightings crashed by up to 99 percent as Burmese pythons spread.
